oneOf.description: The client session's token is missing, invalid, foreign or expired.

scope.description: The scope the method requires; with reason scope, the requested pairing scope the caller does not hold.

reason.description: Present when the method's scope is held and the call is refused all the same: ceiling (it would grant a ceiling above the caller's own: a pairing, or raising another client session), scope (a pairing would grant a scope the caller does not hold, named in data.scope), local (only a local client session may ask it: an artefact path on the environment's machine, the desktop's stage), program (a program client session may not ask it: the known-environments report, whose text reaches every run) or addressed (only the client session a call is addressed to may answer it: client.answer).

ceiling.description: With reason ceiling: the caller's own ceiling, the highest it may grant.

oneOf.description: The client session lacks the scope the method requires, named in data.scope; or, with data.reason ceiling, the call would grant a ceiling above the caller's own, named in data.ceiling; or, with data.reason scope, a pairing would grant a scope the caller does not hold, named in data.scope; or, with data.reason local, only a local client session may ask it; or, with data.reason program, a program client session may not; or, with data.reason addressed, the call is addressed to another client session.

readiness.description: Why the environment cannot answer: it is not ready yet, or it is draining.

oneOf.description: The environment is starting or draining; data.readiness says which.

items.description: One schema issue: a code, the path to the offending value and a message.

oneOf.description: The params or the frame did not match the schema; data.issues lists the schema's issues.
The method's target does not exist.
The target's state does not allow the method now.
The environment failed; nothing the client sent is at fault.

origin.description: A forge origin: https, or http for a LAN or tailnet instance, then the host in lower case and a port only when it is not the scheme's default (https://git.example.com:5526); no userinfo, path or trailing slash.

status.description: The HTTP status the forge answered.

details.description: What the forge answered, behind the message's plain line; absent when the message says it all.

oneOf.description: The forge refused the credential, or answered no user on its identity endpoint (or, listing owners, no list; linking a pull request, no pull request): an add or update stored nothing, a link linked nothing. data names the origin and the HTTP status.

login.description: The login the forge's user endpoint answered, which may change while the user id stays.

userId.description: The forge's numeric user id as decimal digits, a string so that no JSON reader rounds it: what makes a credential the same identity.

expected.description: The identity the credential answers as on the forge account's canonical origin.

login.description: The login the forge's user endpoint answered, which may change while the user id stays.

userId.description: The forge's numeric user id as decimal digits, a string so that no JSON reader rounds it: what makes a credential the same identity.

anyOf.description: Who a forge account's credential answers as: its login and the forge's user id.

found.description: The identity the credential answered as on the alias; null when the alias refused it.

status.description: The HTTP status the alias's identity endpoint answered.

oneOf.description: An alias was not accepted: on its own origin the credential answered as another login or user id than on the forge account's canonical origin, or was refused there, so it is not the same instance. Nothing was changed; data names the alias, both identities and the status.

connectionId.description: The key-manager connection the reference names.

oneOf.description: The key-manager reference could not be read: no key-manager connection on this environment holds it, the connection is not signed in, or the key manager could not be asked now. Nothing was changed; the message says which, and data names the connection.

connectionId.description: The key-manager connection the reference names.

oneOf.description: The key manager holds nothing at the reference's locator: no secret at its path, or no key by its name in the secret. Nothing was changed; data names the connection.

connectionId.description: The key-manager connection the reference names.

oneOf.description: The key manager refused the connection's login the read. OpenBao refuses a path the login may not read, a path that is not there and a mount that is not there alike, so the message says to check the mount first, then the path and the login's policies. Nothing was changed; data names the connection.

connectionId.description: A key-manager connection's id: a version 4 UUID the adding client mints, kept in lowercase.

origin.description: A forge origin: https, or http for a LAN or tailnet instance, then the host in lower case and a port only when it is not the scheme's default (https://git.example.com:5526); no userinfo, path or trailing slash.

kind.description: The kind detection found: gitlab, which no forge account may be added for before milestone 2.

oneOf.description: The URL is on a kind of forge the harness cannot add a forge account for yet (GitLab, milestone 2): data names the origin and the kind.

origin.description: A forge origin: https, or http for a LAN or tailnet instance, then the host in lower case and a port only when it is not the scheme's default (https://git.example.com:5526); no userinfo, path or trailing slash.

oneOf.description: The address answered, and as none of the forges the harness knows (GitHub, Forgejo, Gitea, GitLab) answers on its routes: data names the origin. Name the kind to add a forge account for it anyway.

origin.description: The origin that did not answer.

details.description: What failed, behind the message's plain line: no answer within ten seconds, a lost connection, HTTP 5xx or a rate limit.

oneOf.description: The forge could not be reached, or answered that it could not answer now (its own error, HTTP 5xx; a rate limit; no answer within ten seconds): the message says so plainly and data's details say which; data names the origin.
